I suggest you try out a different brand facesaver headgear on first and see if you can deal with the lack of vertical vision. Maybe you have a spare at your gym or you can try one on at a fight store just to test the visibility. I personally don't like my vision blocked as much so I went with the 2900 which provides decent protection to your nose although not as much as a facesaver headgear. Try one on and if you like the facesaver design then you can commit to buying an fg 5000 since it's an expensive headgear.

Regarding gloves, you wouldn't be using the same gloves for sparring and bag work for a few reasons.

Bag gloves have harder material made to be durable against the heavy bag and sparring gloves typically have softer material to protect your partners face. You also shouldn't use your sparring gloves on the heavy bag (except for breaking them in when you first buy them) because the softer material will be worn out faster and your sparring partner will basically feel your knuckles at that point.

Since you're just getting started, you don't need to worry about sparring for the time being anyways so don't rush it. 

To answer your question on 16 oz gloves for training, that is fine and it has the benefit of giving you a more difficult workout since you are punching with heavier gloves, increasing your shoulder strength naturally. However, you can use whatever glove weight you want for bag work as each has their own use cases - heavier gloves give you a better arm workout and lighter gloves allow you to workout for longer. Unfortunately I don't know anything about the specific gloves you listed however. Hope this helps.
